manifesto.content:
Everyone is talking about AI in quality engineering. *Few are showing the proof.*

We've watched the hype cycle. We've sat through the same demos. We know what an AI-generated test looks like — and we know ==what actually shipped to production== and held up.

Elevate QA exists for the second conversation. The harder one. The one where engineers, leaders, and practitioners put real work on the table — what they tried, what broke, what changed the math.

No vendor pitches. No abstract theory. *The proof of value, or it didn't happen.*

maturity_stages.name: Manual-first
maturity_stages.desc: Test cases authored by hand. Automation islands. AI is "interesting," not yet operational.

maturity_stages.name: Assisted
maturity_stages.desc: AI helps generate test cases and data. Engineers stay in the loop. Early wins, mixed signals.

maturity_stages.name: Augmented
maturity_stages.desc: Self-healing automation, intelligent triage, AI-driven coverage gap analysis. Measurable lift.

maturity_stages.name: Autonomous
maturity_stages.desc: Quality agents reason about risk, prioritize, and adapt. Humans set strategy. The future, already here in pockets.

pillars.title: Keynotes from people doing the work
pillars.desc: Industry voices and engineering leaders sharing concrete case studies — what AI changed, what it cost, what it delivered. Real numbers, not roadmaps.

pillars.title: Practitioner deep-dives
pillars.desc: Hands-on breakouts from engineers who've shipped AI-augmented test suites, self-healing automation, and intelligent quality pipelines at scale.

pillars.title: The community table
pillars.desc: Curated roundtables where 200–500 quality engineering leaders connect, debate, and forge the relationships that move careers and companies forward.

pillars.title: Live demos, not slideware
pillars.desc: See AI-led QE tooling in action on real codebases, real bugs, real flaky tests. Working software is the only honest demo.

pillars.title: The candid panels
pillars.desc: The unfiltered conversations: what AI in QE is overhyped, what's underrated, where the field goes from here. Speakers who'll say it plainly.

pillars.title: Recognition & prizes
pillars.desc: Speaker of the event, audience awards, and surprises throughout the day. We celebrate the people pushing the field — loudly.

speaker_applications.name: Sanjay Kumar
speaker_applications.topic: From Pain Points to Productivity: Smarter Testing With and Without AI
speaker_applications.bio: Sanjay Kumar is the founder and creator of SelectorsHub and a suite of free productivity tools for testers. Built with zero funding and powered by the QA community, his tools empower over 1.8 million testers to solve real-world challenges faster and smarter every day.

speaker_applications.name: Khushi Aggarwal
speaker_applications.topic: BattleTest: Autonomous Adversarial Testing Using AI Red Team, Blue Team & Judge Agents
speaker_applications.bio: I am a Software QA Engineer with experience in manual, automation, API, and database testing, primarily within the CPQ domain. I work with Robot Framework, Python, APIs, and databases to ensure software quality and reliability. I enjoy learning new technologies, building new skills, and exploring innovative approaches to testing. I'm particularly excited about how AI is transforming Quality Engineering.

speaker_applications.bio: My name is Neha Pal, a software developer passionate about building innovative and scalable applications. I have experience with Java, Spring Boot, Flask, Node.js, React, and MySQL. I enjoy solving technical challenges, learning new technologies, and developing secure, efficient solutions, particularly in real-time communication and web application development.

speaker_applications.name: Baljap Singh
speaker_applications.topic: Leveraging AI in QA tasks (QA Dashboard for test case generation, Test Case generation and reporting using MCP)
speaker_applications.bio: Baljap Singh is a Software Development Engineer in Test (SDET) specializing in backend testing, API automation, and quality engineering for distributed systems. He works extensively with Java, REST Assured, Kafka, Elasticsearch, and cloud-native technologies to build scalable and reliable testing solutions. Passionate about continuous learning, Baljap actively explores emerging areas such as Artificial Intelligence, AI agents, and modern developer tooling to enhance software quality and engineering productivity. He is particularly interested in the intersection of AI and testing, focusing on how intelligent systems can transform automation and quality assurance practices. Baljap enjoys sharing knowledge, collaborating with the tech community, and contributing to discussions around modern testing, automation, and AI-driven engineering.

speaker_applications.name: Sagar Ravikiran Joshi
speaker_applications.topic: Testing the “Non-Testable”: Metamorphic Testing in Practice
speaker_applications.bio:
Sagar Joshi is a software testing professional, trainer, and quality engineering leader with over 16 years of experience in the automotive and enterprise software domains. Having worked with organisations such as Bosch, TCS, and KPIT, he has led testing teams and driven quality initiatives across complex, large-scale projects. He specialises in test strategy, test management, and building strong testing foundations that remain relevant despite evolving technologies.

He is the founder of SAJO Academy Private Limited, where he delivers ISTQB® certification programmes and industry-focused training to professionals and corporate teams worldwide. A holder of multiple ISTQB certifications, along with PMP and Agile credentials, SAJO is passionate about helping testers move beyond tools and trends to develop lasting engineering thinking. He is also the author of Software Testing Essentials – An ISTQB® Foundation Guide, aimed at strengthening practical understanding of software testing fundamentals.

speaker_applications.name: Krati shukla
speaker_applications.bio:
Hi, I am Krati Shukla, a Software QA Engineer at SDET Tech with experience in the eCommerce and FinTech domains. My expertise includes manual testing, API testing, and test automation using Robot Framework and Selenium. I am passionate about leveraging AI in software testing and enjoy exploring innovative AI-driven solutions that improve testing efficiency and automate repetitive processes.

I am Rajat Aggarwal, a Software Test Trainee with experience in manual testing, test automation and workflow automation. I have worked on AEM-based digital experience platforms and enterprise web applications, gaining hands-on expertise in Playwright, Selenium, Java, TypeScript, Azure DevOps, and n8n. I am passionate about exploring AI-driven solutions that improve productivity and reduce manual effort in software development and testing processes.

speaker_applications.name: Rajat Aggarwal
speaker_applications.company: SDET Tech Pvt. Ltd. - Software Testing Company
speaker_applications.bio: I am Rajat Aggarwal, a Software Test Trainee with a strong interest in Test Automation and AI-powered solutions. I have hands-on experience with Playwright, TypeScript, Node.js, Jira, REST APIs, and Microsoft Graph API. I developed NoteBridge AI, an intelligent AI agent that automates Microsoft Teams meeting participation, generates meeting transcripts using Whisper AI, analyzes discussions with Llama 3, and automatically updates Jira tickets. Through this presentation, I will demonstrate how AI can automate software engineering workflows, reduce manual effort, improve productivity, and streamline bug triage and project management. I am passionate about learning emerging technologies and building practical automation solutions that solve real-world challenges.

speaker_applications.name: Raneesh Choudhary
speaker_applications.topic: Code Review Is the New Engineering Bottleneck
speaker_applications.bio: Raneesh has spent 9 years in the wild world of software testing. I specialize in dissecting requirements, crafting test strategies that actually work, and building automation frameworks that don’t crumble under pressure. Oh, and when I’m not busy breaking things (intentionally, of course), I try to share what I have learned through courses, workshops, blogs, or whatever works.
